en.html:
Where I woke up, I had never been before.
A white room. Clean-looking. Not large—six mats at most—but with so few things in it, the emptiness had somehow become spacious.

The plain bed I had just left was practically the only object insisting on its existence. One chair, a few small items. That was the remaining population.

Look again: not even a window. Of course I felt suffocated. There was a vent. For the lungs, perhaps adequate. For the mind, absolutely not.

My head felt packed with lead. Before any thinking could be done, it demanded to be taken out of this place.
I found a door in one corner and walked toward it.
Only a few steps, and I stumbled several times. For some reason, my hands and feet had very little feeling.
As though somebody else's body had been handed to me, to operate by string. Somehow I reached the door, took the knob, turned it and pulled.

ja.html:
目覚めたそこは、未知の場所だった。

　白く、清潔感のある部屋だ。
　広くはない。せいぜい六畳だろう。だが物が少ない
せいか、やけに空漠として見える。

　存在感を有する物体は、たった今まで我が身を横た
えていた質素な<ruby>寝台<rt>ベッド</rt></ruby>くらいしかない。
　後は椅子が一つと、小物が数点。

　見直せば、壁に窓すら無かった。
　息苦しさを覚えるのは間違いなくそのせいだろう。
通風孔はあるが、身体的にはともかく心理的には全く
必要充分でない。

　鉛を詰めたように重い頭蓋は、考えを巡らせる前に
まずここから出る事を要求していた。
　
　部屋の一隅に扉を見つけ、そちらに歩く。

　ほんの数歩を進むために、幾度かよろめいた。
　どういうわけか、手足の感覚が鈍い。

　他人の体を糸で操っている心地になりながら、どう
にか辿り着く。
　<ruby>把手<rt>ノブ</rt></ruby>を掴んで、回して引いた。

en.html:
Achha. One new fact had presented itself.
The door did not open. Locked. From outside, naturally.

I inspected the handle from every possible angle. Keyhole? None. Button? None. Trigger? Nothing. It was not opening.
Therefore, I was a prisoner.

...No. Let us not become hasty intellectuals.
It could simply be a hospital room. Perhaps the lock kept unauthorized people out. Certain patients might need rooms they could not open from inside, no?

A prisoner and a patient could both be told to stay in bed. The important difference was whether somebody wished you to recover or wished you to remain available. A very large distinction, and this door was offering no assistance with it. From the door's point of view, apparently, I belonged on this side. Bas. No interest in my professional classification.

If that was the case, one thing to do first. Inform the outside world that I had woken up.

さて。
　状況が新たに一つ判明した。

　扉は開かない。
　鍵が掛けられている。無論、外側から。

　把手を舐めるように見回してみようが、鍵穴もなけ
ればボタンも引き金もない。
　開ける事は不可能だった。

　つまり監禁されている。

　……いや。
　決め付けるのは早計か。

　ここは単に病院の病室であり、鍵が掛かっているの
は関係者以外の立ち入りを禁ずる為なのかもしれない。
　患者の症状によっては、内側から開けられない部屋
に収容する必要もあるだろう。

　で、あれば――とりあえず、すべきは一つだ。
　起床した事実を外へ伝えよう。

en.html:
That seemed to be the situation.

If I claimed to have no idea why, amnesia would be a reasonable accusation. I had opposed GHQ officers on Enoshima. Not enough time had passed for that memory to quietly retire.

Silver Star had arrived and ended the whole business in chaos, yes. But why should GHQ suddenly decide, never mind, leave Kageaki alone? Their next move was only natural.

Still, this was very sudden. No connection, and here I was. That explanation did not account for everything.
No connection...?

Connection.
I had been going to Kenchouji to save the Prince and the others...
Yes. The attack on Kenchouji. So that had been————the Occupation's...?
Then that, also—

en.html:
.......................................................
Even calling aloud produced no answering ring of metal. Could she not hear? Or was she hearing, but unable to answer...?

A rare situation. Rare did not mean good.
A wielder and a tsurugi, once bonded, were one warrior between them. One being, you could say. Separation should not be possible.
Far beyond sight of one another, we could still speak as though side by side.
Now, nothing.

The most likely explanation: she had lost the power to speak.
In other words, complete destruction.
The dead could not answer. Even a tsurugi, which was not so easy to classify as a living creature, could not get an exception from that rule.

　聴こえていないのか、聴こえていても答えられない

　これは稀有な事態だ。
　無論、良からぬ意味で。

　縁を結んだ仕手と劒冑は二人で一騎の武者となる。

は両者が引き離される事など<ruby>有り得ない<rt>・・・・・</rt></ruby>。

　互いが見えないほど距離を隔てていても、隣にいる
のと同様に通話できるのだ。
　
　それが今はできない。

　最も妥当な可能性は、会話する能力を失ったという
それだ。

　つまり、完全に破壊された。

　死者に口無し。
　一概に生物とは定義し難い劒冑とて、その格言から
逃れられはしない。

en.html:
—The only other possibility I could think of was an isolation box, a device sealing off communication. But would GHQ take such trouble over Muramasa—over us, whom they had wanted removed as an obstruction? Very doubtful.

Still... I was alive. This body, invaded by tetrodotoxin, was alive. If Muramasa had healed me, she must have been all right until at least that work was finished...

Whatever the truth, I had no way to check it now.
Wait for something to happen. Freedom gone, no means of getting it back: that left me one choice.
Some choice. I did not much care to honor it with the name.

I returned to the bed and lay down, still heavy with exhaustion. Do the best available. At present, lying down was the best available.

――それ以外には、<ruby>通信遮断装置<rt>アイソレーションボックス</rt></ruby>に密封されている
可能性くらいしか思い当たらないが。
　ＧＨＱが邪魔者として始末しようとした<ruby>村正<rt>おれ</rt></ruby>の為に
そこまでの手間を掛けるものかどうか、大いに疑問だ。

　ただ……<ruby>猛毒<rt>テトロドトキシン</rt></ruby>に冒されたこの肉体が生存している。
　村正が回復させたのだとすれば、少なくともそれが
終了するまでは健在だったという事になる……。

　いずれにしろ、今は事実を確認できる状態にない。

　動きが起こるのを待つしかないだろう。
　自由を奪われ、その自由を取り戻す方法もない以上、
それが唯一の選択だ。

　……そんな事を選択などと呼びたくはないが。
　
　俺はせめてもの最善を尽くすべく、ベッドに戻って
いまだ疲れが濃く残る身体を横たえた。
